sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Urban Electric Cargo Bicycles and Step-Through Scooters

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Unitary National legal system; continental civil law tradition codified in the Code civil and Code de commerce)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Franco-Chinese Bilateral Investment Treaty of 30 May 1984 (in force since 26 June 1985; guarantees fair and equitable treatment, free transfer of capital, and access to ICSID and ICC arbitration)

Double Taxation Agreement between France and the People's Republic of China of 26 November 2013 (in force since 1 January 2015; reduces dividend withholding to 5% subject to limitation-on-benefits conditions)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (concluded in principle on 30 December 2020; ratification currently suspended pending post-2023 EU political review)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI; applicable to the France-China DTA and broadly to the French treaty network)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier - CMF), Articles L.561-1 to L.561-58 (AML/CFT obligations), Article L.561-45 et seq. (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs - RBE), Articles L.562-1 to L.562-11 (financial restrictive measures and asset freezes), and Articles L.574-1 to L.574-4 (criminal penalties). Implementing texts include Décret n°2020-118 of 12 February 2020 (RBE content and filing technicalities), Décret n°2021-1621 of 9 December 2021 (extension of RBE duties to foreign companies' French branches), and the French transposition of Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD). Law n°2021-1308 of 8 October 2021 (loi anti-organised crime) reinforced RBE transparency and TRACFIN powers. The SAS legal form is governed by Articles L.227-1 to L.227-23 of the French Commercial Code.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport page of each natural-person shareholder/UBO and each proposed statutory director of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of each person's country of nationality (e.g., National Immigration Administration of the People's Republic of China)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Clean criminal record certificate or police clearance certificate (extrait de casier judiciaire / 无犯罪记录证明) of each proposed director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public Security Bureau of the person's habitual Chinese residence or the equivalent competent police authority of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Official certificate of incorporation or current commercial register extract of every non-natural-person shareholder in the SAS's direct or indirect control chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation of the PRC or the equivalent company registry of each shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration evidencing the lawful origin of the equity capital contribution to the French SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Shareholder's primary relationship bank (e.g., Bank of China, ICBC, CMB, or other licensed commercial bank)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of all apostilled documents and of the draft SAS statuts by a translator registered with a French Cour d'appel (traducteur assermenté)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Court-appointed certified translator on the national list of judicial experts

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO (natural person holding 25% or more of capital or voting rights), all statutory directors and all fronting signatories against (i) the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (ii) the EU Council consolidated restrictive measures list; (iii) the OFAC SDN list and the 50% aggregate ownership rule; (iv) the French financial sanctions list maintained by the Direction Générale du Trésor (MEF-IGF); and (v) French and international PEP databases, including judicial records and the Fichier Judiciaire des Auteurs d'Infractions Terroristes. Under Articles L.561-6 and R.561-1 CMF, simplified due diligence may be applied for a low-risk manufacturing entity, but enhanced due diligence is triggered by any PEP disposition, any FATF-high-risk jurisdiction shareholder, any adverse media hit, or any irregularity in the apostilled documents. Continuous monitoring at least annually and upon any change in ownership of the threshold is mandatory; corporate services providers, business-centre domiciliation entities and opening banks in France will independently re-run the screening prior to Kbis issuance and bank account activation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) - electronic filing portal accessible at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; prior name and trademark collision verification performed through data.inpi.fr and the RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés) database maintained by the Greffes des tribunaux de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under French Law n°94-665 of 4 August 1994 (loi Toubon), the SAS name must be expressed in French or in roman script legible to a French public reader; where a Chinese-origin brand is adopted, a standardized Pinyin transliteration and, where appropriate, a French-language descriptor (manufacture de vélos à assistance électrique, mobilité urbaine) must be embedded in the statuts and in the Annonce Légale. The name must be uniform across the statuts, the registration filing, the legal gazette publication and the RCS; any term suggesting a larger entity, financial institution or public body is barred unless the corporate purpose materially supports it.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: French law does not operate a pre-incorporation name reservation registry in the common-law sense; the name becomes opposable upon publication of the Annonce Légale and entry in the RCS. If the Guichet Unique rejects the filing or the Greffe refuses registration because the name is contrary to public policy, misleading, or collides with an earlier trademark or firm name, the founder may (i) file a rectified dossier naming a substituted denotation within 15 calendar days via the Guichet Unique; (ii) address a formal request for reconsideration to the INPI help desk competent for the file; (iii) appeal the Greffe's refusal to the President of the Tribunal de commerce of the registered department in summary proceedings within two months of notification, citing Article R.123-164 of the Code de commerce; and (iv) concurrently file an INVPI trademark application or an opposition to any blocking earlier mark. The most efficient path is an ex-ante clearance opinion covering French, EU and Chinese earlier rights before any filing is submitted, combined with a primary and a reserve name statement.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible for the pre-operational and commercial stage: a SAS may validly be domiciled at a regulated business centre or an approved domiciliation company under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code for a maximum of five years, renewable, subject to genuine access and effective direction. However, for an ISIC 3091 electric cargo bicycle manufacturing and step-through scooter OEM operation, a purely virtual office will not satisfy corporate substance reviews by the French tax authorities, customs (DGDDI), URSSAF, or the manufacturing regulators where physical assembly, quality control, warehouse and after-sales operations are performed; the company must transition to a physical operational site in accordance with its industrial plan.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 12% estimated probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 24 months for a low-risk manufacturing SME, based on the combined inspection frequencies of DGFiP (tax field visits under Articles L.13 and L.16B of the Livre des procédures fiscales), URSSAF, DGCCRF and DGDDI; the probability rises to approximately 45% where there is an atypical VAT refund claim, a customs valuation query, a B2B complaint, or an inconsistency between the declared headcount and the physical office substance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: INPI Guichet Unique incorporation fee - SAS registration in the RCS and issuance of SIRENE/SIRET identifiers through the single formalities portal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI) - Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff fixed by INPI decree (approximately EUR 250), payable through the Guichet Unique; includes the RCS file creation and the SIRENE/SIRET data entry

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory publication of the incorporation notice (annonce légale) in a legal gazette admitted by the competent judicial authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: JAL-allowed legal gazette publisher in the registered department (e.g., Les Echos, Affiches Parisiennes for Paris and Petite Couronne)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-line price fixed by the département authority, approximately EUR 154-EUR 196 in the Paris region including VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille bundle for the Chinese-origin UBO dossier (police clearances, passport copies, business registration extract of each corporate shareholder)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Consular Division) or the authorised local Foreign Affairs Office; where applicable, French Consulate General in the place of signature
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document apostille fee (approximately RMB 50-RMB 100 per criminal record certificate / passport / extract) plus courier and administrative handling costs for a standard 3-4 document set

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of the apostilled UBO documents and the draft SAS statuts by a traducteur assermenté registered with a French Cour d'appel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-appointed certified translator on the national list of judicial experts
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of EUR 40-EUR 60 per 2,500-character standard page; estimated 8-10 pages for a full dossier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance, pre-availability verification and prior-mark collision analysis covering French, EU and Chinese earlier rights for the cargo e-bike brand (classes 12, 35, 39 and 42)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an availability opinion covering data.inpi.fr, TMview and a professional trademark database search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO control-chain piercing memorandum identifying all natural persons owning 25% or more in every intermediate corporate layer, including look-through of any trust, nominee or holding arrangement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Time-based market benchmark of 3-5 hours of senior counsel review at discounted flat arrangement for the pre-incorporation stage

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening of all UBOs and statutory directors against the UN, EU, OFAC, TRACFIN and French national financial sanctions lists, including a 12-month rescreening subscription
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed AML/KYC software provider or external compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat per-person fee per list searched, with monthly automated rescreening and manual negative-media verification

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation service - 12-month agreement with a regulated domiciliation company providing the attestation required for Kbis issuance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Regulated domiciliataire authorised under Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a business centre in Paris or Petite Couronne of EUR 300-EUR 500 per year plus VAT

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of the SAS statuts, RBE annex and internal governance rules adapted to a non-resident foreign shareholder and foreign-director appointment structure
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Flat fee market benchmark for a single-class SAS with private deed execution, no employee matters and standard governance provisions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Signature authentication and consular/notarial verification of the executed statuts where the foreign shareholder signs in China (optional but risk-reducing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French notary, Consulate General of France in the shareholder's place of residence, or Chinese notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial and consular fee schedule of approximately EUR 50-EUR 110 per signing session plus RMB notary rates where applicable

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS régime); R.227-1 et seq.; joint provisions L.210-1 to L.210-10 and R.210-1 to R.210-9; Décret n° 2019-514 implementing the Law of 22 March 2019 (relative à la création des sociétés et aux procédures de signalement).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court), operating exclusively through the national single digital portal 'formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr'.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) together with the unified 'Déclaration de création d'une société' (single incorporation form, formerly Cerfa M0); filing recorded with the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for SAS. Capital must be fully subscribed by shareholders and, if contributed in cash, deposited in a blocked escrow account opened with a French or EU bank; a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) issued by the bank is required. If the capital is less than EUR 50,000, the schedule for releasing contributions may be fixed in the statuts; any capital equal to or above EUR 50,000 requires immediate full payment of cash contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the inaugural meeting of the sole shareholder and acting as the governance body of the SAS, it is resolved that: (1) the share capital as stated in the statuts is hereby subscribed in full by the shareholder, and the cash contribution has been deposited into the company's blocked account; (2) the registered office is established at the address indicated in Article 4 of the statuts; (3) the following officers are appointed: President of the SAS, General Manager if necessary, and the statutory auditor where legally required; (4) all necessary incorporation filings are approved and the President is authorized to execute and file the incorporation dossier with the competent registry; and (5) the officers undertake to open a business bank account and to comply with all French commercial, tax and social obligations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Shareholders and legal counsel; notarization, if required, by a French notary public.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS statuts in French containing at least: corporate name, registered office address, corporate purpose, share capital and classes of shares, identity of the president (and directors, if any), approval of asset contributions, in-kind contributions and special benefits, and provisions on decisions of the shareholders. The statuts must be dated and signed by all shareholders (or by the sole shareholder acting as sole associate). If the registered office is located in hired premises, provide the occupancy evidence (lease, lease agreement or access agreement). If any contribution in kind is included, the commissaire aux apports must issue a valuation report prior to signature.
required_dossiers: Draft and final signed copy of the statuts
Certificate of identity of each shareholder (passport or national ID card)
Company name availability certificate (if any) or proof of no identical trademark
Occupancy document for the registered office address
Valuation report of in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the statuts are rejected for incompleteness, rectify the noted omissions and resubmit online within the portal; if an in-kind valuation report is missing, engage a commissaire aux apports and supplement the dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Share Capital in a Blocked Escrow Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French commercial bank or French branch of an EU credit institution; Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations for unpaid capital not released to the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company-in-formation and transfer at least the total amount of cash capital subscribed. The bank will issue an 'attestation de dépôt de fonds' containing the amount, account details and the names of the deposit subscribers. If the capital exceeds EUR 50,000 or the statuts require full payment, the funds remain blocked until incorporation. After the registrar issues the compliance certificate (RCS registration), the bank releases the funds to the company by producing the K-bis extract.
required_dossiers: The signed statuts (deposit copy)
Identity of the shareholders
Bank-provided deposit certificate (attestation de dépôt de fonds)
Power of attorney, if signing by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to release funds after registration, provide the official K-bis extract and reissue the attestation; in case of a delayed attestation, request a written refusal and file a complaint with the bank's compliance department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish an Incorporation Notice in a Legal Gazette (Annonce Légale)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (e.g. Actu-Juridique, Petites Affiches, or any authorized legal gazette); longest-lived French newspaper or specialized online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a mandatory legal notice (avis de constitution) containing the corporate name, corporate form, share capital, registered office, corporate object summary, duration, and the names of the directors. The notice is published in the department of the registered office. Obtain a certified copy of the publication (attestation de parution) issued by the gazette, which must be submitted with the incorporation dossier.
required_dossiers: Draft notice text
Corporate details as per statuts
Gazette-provided attestation of publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If gazette publication is delayed or rejected, choose an alternative authorized legal journal in the same département and reissue the notice; ensure the notice date precedes the registry filing within the statutory 8-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce via the single portal 'formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr'.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the unified 'Déclaration de création d'une société' on formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, attach the signed statuts, proof of identity of each shareholder, the deposit certificate, the gazette publication attestation, proof of the registered office address, and any additional declarations (e.g., clearances from regulated professions, if applicable). Submit the dossier and pay the registry fee by card or other accepted electronic means. The registry will review the dossier and, if compliant, issue the K-bis extract (RCS registration certificate) and legal existence.
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (one certified true copy)
Certificate of deposit of share capital
Proof of gazette publication
Proof of identity of each shareholder and officer
Proof of registered office occupation
Completed and signed declaration of non-conviction (declaration sur l'honneur) for managing officers
Mandatory declaration of controllership (liste des personnes exerçant le contrôle) if applicable
Single form / creator's details
Case-by-case additional documents (e.g., notarized powers if a proxy signs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry raises a query, address the requested corrections within the prescribed deadline (usually 15 days) by uploading amended documents to the portal. Inactive dossier for more than 2 months may be returned; resubmit with a fresh declaration. If formal refusal, request consultation with the Greffe or the RCS officer, or file a petition before the court (juge des référés).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain K-bis Extract, Register with the Tax and Social Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: The same Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (for K-bis); Le Centre des Finances Publiques / Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFIP) and Urssaf via the INPI portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the K-bis extract, verify that the corporate data is accurate. The registry transmits the incorporation data to the tax and social authorities automatically: the DGFIP assigns a SIREN and SIRET number, the tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises - SIE) opens a corporate tax file, and the Urssaf assigns a business social security account. Apply for the ACT (Auxiliairies de Commerce) or continue regular tax status; if value-added tax (VAT) is applicable, request the intra-community VAT number on form 3310 via the SIE. Sign the French national e-invoicing (Factur-X) scheme once effective.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Completed SIE forms (e.g., 21 for corporations) for tax registration
VAT application (Form 3310 CA3ER) if relevant
Declaration of business bank account (RIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If IRS/tax registration does not occur within the normal SLA, contact the SIE directly with the K-bis; if the SIREN is already assigned, request immediate reactivation of the tax file. For missing SIRET, verify the company's address in the national directory (INSEE).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) and the Prefecture of the department where the factory is located; the Ministry of Ecological Transition for ICPE approvals.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation / Enregistrement / Déclaration d'exploitation d'une Installation Classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE), rubrique 2940 (appréciation des métaux pour traitement de surface, only if applicable) and/or rubrique 2925 (atelier de charge d'accumulateurs); for simple assembly operations, a 'Déclaration' regime applies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition écologique, de l'Énergie, du Climat et de la Prévention des risques; DREAL as local delegated authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Régime de la Déclaration) under ICPE category 2925 for battery-charging stations and category 2940 only if surface treatment is performed; a full 'Étude d'impact' is not required for typical light-assembly e-bike manufacturing without significant discharges. An environmental prohibition exemption is granted if scrap, oil, solvents and packaged storage remain below regulatory thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater pH 6.5–8.5; Chemical Oxygen Demand < 125 mg/L; Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD5) < 25 mg/L; Total Suspended Solids < 35 mg/L; volatile organic compounds (VOCs) < 50 mg C/Nm³ in ventilated air; hazardous waste must be disposed exclusively through licensed treatment channels; all storage of lithium-ion batteries must adhere to the NF EN 50604-1 standard and fire-resistance limitations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification delivered by the Service Départemental d'Incendie et de Secours (SDIS) for the assembly plant, battery storage room and maintenance bay; structural certificate from the local urban planning office or building health and safety commission (CODERST) verifying load capacity; workplace clearance by the inspection du travail (labour inspectorate) for occupational health and safety compliance, including the registration of the operations in the 'Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques' (DUERP) and compliance with EU machine safety directives (2006/42/EC).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction générale des Finances publiques (DGFiP), including the relevant Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) and the official impots.gouv.fr portal. Corporate formation and unified business registration are administered through the Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SAS, submit the incorporation and beneficial-owner information through the INPI Guichet unique. The registry process generates the SIREN identifier for the legal entity and SIRET identifier for each establishment; the entity is then recorded in the Registre national des entreprises. Open the corporate tax account with the competent SIE through impots.gouv.fr and provide the articles of association, registration extract, registered-office evidence, director identification, beneficial-owner filing, business activity description, bank details, and foreign shareholder documentation where applicable. Obtain the French VAT identification number from the DGFiP after VAT registration or confirmation of VAT liability; the number generally consists of the country prefix FR followed by a two-digit key and the nine-digit SIREN. A non-established foreign entity must apply to the competent non-resident tax service or designated SIE before commencing taxable French transactions, unless an applicable intermediary or special registration rule applies. Obtain an Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number through French customs for import or export customs operations. Registration does not itself establish a permanent establishment; that determination follows French domestic law and applicable tax treaties.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SAS is generally subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). There is no US-style check-the-box regime and no general French election to classify an SAS as a fiscally transparent entity. Subject to statutory conditions, an SAS may elect temporary taxation under personal income tax rules for up to five financial years. The election generally requires that the company be created for less than five years, conduct an eligible commercial, industrial, artisanal, or professional activity, be unlisted, remain below the applicable employee and turnover or balance-sheet limits, and satisfy ownership and management participation requirements, including specified individual ownership and management thresholds. The election requires unanimous shareholder approval and notification to the tax administration within the prescribed period. A family-company election available to certain partnerships does not generally apply to an SAS. France has anti-hybrid-mismatch rules implementing ATAD II; these are statutory denial or inclusion rules, not elective entity-classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French value added tax (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, VAT), harmonized with the European Union VAT system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a French business supplying goods, including manufactured electric cargo bicycles and step-through scooters, the domestic franchise en base de TVA generally applies below EUR 85,000 annual turnover, subject to the applicable prior-year and current-year thresholds and statutory tolerance rules. A higher threshold of EUR 93,500 generally applies as the current-year tolerance limit for goods activities. The thresholds are distinct from the service thresholds of EUR 37,500 and EUR 41,250. VAT registration is also required irrespective of the small-business threshold for transactions or situations for which the franchise is unavailable, including certain intra-Community acquisitions, imports, and transactions giving rise to French VAT liability. EU cross-border SME exemption rules may apply only if their separate Union-wide and national conditions are satisfied.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing mandatory electronic invoicing and electronic transaction reporting in phases. From 1 September 2026, all French-established businesses must be able to receive compliant electronic invoices through a registered Platform for Electronic Invoicing (Plateforme agréée), formerly referred to as a Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP); issuance obligations apply first to large companies and tax groups, with small and medium-sized enterprises generally entering the issuance phase from 1 September 2027. Business-to-government invoicing continues through the Chorus Pro system. The French model is not a universal real-time pre-clearance system: invoices are transmitted through an approved platform, while required transaction and payment data are reported to the tax administration. Invoices must contain mandatory French and EU VAT information, permit structured electronic processing, and support archiving, authenticity, integrity, and auditability. Imports and exports remain subject to customs electronic systems and EORI requirements. Timing and technical specifications remain subject to implementing legislation and official DGFiP guidance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods dispatched or transported from France to a destination outside the European Union may qualify for VAT exemption under the French implementation of the EU VAT rules, provided the supplier establishes that the goods actually left the EU customs territory and satisfies invoicing, accounting, customs, and documentary requirements. The supplier must generally be the exporter or act through an authorized exporter and must retain the export declaration and electronic customs exit evidence, together with commercial and transport records linking the goods, customer, invoice, and shipment. A sale to an EU customer is generally not an export: it may qualify as an exempt intra-Community supply only where the customer has a valid VAT number in another Member State, the goods are transported to that Member State, the reporting requirements are met, and the supplier holds evidence of transport. B2B services supplied to a business established outside France are generally outside the scope of French VAT under the place-of-supply rule rather than technically zero-rated; exceptions apply to services connected with immovable property, passenger transport, events, short-term vehicle hire, and other special categories. Input VAT may be recovered through French VAT returns where the statutory deduction conditions are met. Export exemption or input-tax recovery may be denied where evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, late, or connected with fraud.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic export customs declaration accepted by French customs, including the Movement Reference Number or equivalent declaration reference
Electronic confirmation of exit from the European Union customs territory, such as the Export Accompanying Document and exit results
Commercial invoice identifying the French supplier, customer, goods, value, delivery terms, and export transaction
Packing list and transport documentation, including bill of lading, airway bill, CMR, or equivalent carrier evidence
Evidence linking the goods and invoice to the shipment, including purchase order, sales contract, serial or batch records where relevant, and proof of delivery or destination
EORI number and customs representation or power-of-attorney records where a customs agent is used
For an intra-Community supply rather than an export, the customer's valid EU VAT identification number, recapitulative statement data, and documentary proof of transport to another Member State
Banking and accounting records supporting consideration and transaction reconciliation; an inward-remittance certificate is not generally a mandatory French export-VAT document
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: France has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. Export VAT exemption is substantiated primarily by customs exit and transport evidence, not by a mandatory foreign-exchange repatriation certificate. If the goods did not leave the EU, the evidence is deficient, or the exemption was fraudulently claimed, the DGFiP may reassess VAT, recover improperly refunded or deducted input VAT, charge late-payment interest, and impose tax penalties. The penalty may generally be 40% for deliberate failure, 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abuse of rights, and 80% for fraudulent activity, subject to statutory conditions and procedural safeguards; other penalties may apply for inaccurate invoices, missing records, or reporting failures. Customs duties, import VAT, customs penalties, and joint or representative liability may also arise. Criminal prosecution may apply in serious tax-fraud cases. Clawback periods are generally governed by French VAT limitation periods, commonly three years, with longer periods possible in specified fraudulent or criminal circumstances.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) — French central bank and Eurosystem member acting as national competent authority for TARGET2, payment statistics and balance-of-payments reporting; the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance exercises exchange-control policy, foreign-exchange regulation and foreign investment screening; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) licenses and supervises credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic-money institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is in the euro area and is fully liberalised under Articles 63–64 TFEU: the euro is freely convertible for current and capital account operations, and the French SAS has no exchange-control restriction on receiving export proceeds, paying import obligations, servicing trade debt or distributing dividends to non-resident shareholders. The only functional hurdles are: (i) the Banque de France balance-of-payments declaration for each cross-border transaction exceeding EUR 12,500, filed by the executing bank on the company's behalf; (ii) the French dividend withholding tax regime for distributions to foreign shareholders (standard 30% or treaty-reduced rate; EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption at 0% when the EU parent holds at least 10% of the SAS for a continuous two-year period and the intermediary holding conditions are met); and (iii) EU sanctions and the FDI screening rules of Articles L151-1 to L151-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, which do not cover an electric cargo bicycle/ISIC 3091 manufacturer and therefore permit unrestricted inbound capital injection and outward profit remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. France imposes no surrender or mandatory conversion of export receipts; the SAS may hold export receivables in EUR, USD, CNY or any other currency on a free account with an authorised bank or abroad. For statistical compliance: (i) each payment instruction or receipt above EUR 12,500 executed with a resident bank is reported by the bank in the Banque de France single balance-of-payments return; (ii) intra-EU merchandise dispatches above the annual threshold of EUR 460,000 must be lodged via the DEB (Déclaration d'Échanges de Biens) by the 10th working day of the following month; (iii) extra-EU export dispatches are captured by the customs export declaration (DAU) and the EU Export Control System; and (iv) any foreign bank account held by the SAS or its controlling shareholders must be declared annually on French tax form 3916.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Financial Statements and Corporate Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties of 0.5% of the tax due per month of delay (maximum 5 years), possible criminal sanctions including imprisonment, and administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if two or more of the following are exceeded: turnover exceeding 800,000 EUR, total assets exceeding 400,000 EUR, or average number of employees exceeding 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information is declared at incorporation and updated upon changes; no separate annual confirmation required

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0-500 USD (self-managed registered office or professional service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (no audit required) to 5,000-15,000 USD (if audit mandated, depending on company size)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% rate on first €42,500 of taxable income for qualifying SMEs; R&D tax credit up to 30% of eligible expenses; accelerated depreciation allowances

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200-A (Corporate Income Tax Return) via impots.gouv.fr electronic portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., 31 March for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before tax credits and adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents: income from French source must be declared; permanent establishment adjustments required
Participation exemption may apply to French-sourced dividends if 5% threshold met and conditions fulfilled

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: €150 fixed penalty plus 0.75% of tax due per month of delay, capped at 10% of tax; criminal prosecution possible for fraudulent filings

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain and submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to French tax authorities; file application for treaty benefits on impots.gouv.fr; provide beneficial ownership declaration
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 10% (e.g. 5% for industrial property under many treaties); Interest: 12.8% statutory rate, reduced to 0% under most double tax treaties if debt is at arm's length

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50,000,000 consolidated group revenue for local file requirement
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: French Economic Substance Regulations require relevant activities and adequate resources for entities claiming tax benefits in France, particularly for holding companies and IP regimes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional false declaration of income or expenses to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of up to 5 years and fine of up to 80% of the evaded tax; repayment of taxes with interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for criminal sanctions including imprisonment and potential disqualification; civil liability for restitution

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to document or apply arm's length principle in intra-group transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of up to €10 million or 5% of annual turnover; possible criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and imprisonment for willful non-compliance; potential jail time

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French entity without sufficient operational or managerial substance for claimed tax positions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of tax positions; denial of deductions; fines up to €1 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability with possible imprisonment; director disqualification and bans

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring profit repatriation to evade reporting or taxes through shell entities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years; asset seizure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for directors involved in fraudulent schemes; possible travel bans and asset freezes
